stories.title: Manga Hotel Group Acquires Royal Sonesta Chicago River North
stories.excerpt: Manga Hotel Group announced the acquisition of the Royal Sonesta Chicago River North, a 261-room hotel located in Chicago, Illinois. The hotel has been rebranded as Hotel 505 River North, an independent property which is slated to become the site of another TOOR Hotel.Located at 505 North State Street in downtown Chicago, the hotel is surrounded by dining, entertainment, shopping and cultural attractions, with convenient access to the Magnificent Mile. Following acquisitions in New York City of the SoHo 54 Hotel last year and The Chelsean New York Hotel in June, this acquisition further expands Manga’s growing portfolio in the United States and marks its entry into the Chicago market. “We are excited to mark another important milestone in the continued expansion of TOOR Hotel,” says Sukhdev Toor, President and CEO of Manga Hotel Group, “Chicago is an important hospitality market, and this was a strategic move to add another major city to the TOOR brand alongside Toronto and New York City.” The post Manga Hotel Group Acquires Royal Sonesta Chicago River North appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Manga Hotel Group acquires 261-room Royal Sonesta Chicago River North, rebrands as Hotel 505.
Hotel conversion marks Manga's entry into Chicago market after NYC acquisitions.
Property located 505 North State Street, downtown River North near Magnificent Mile.
stories.summary: Manga Hotel Group acquired the 261-room Royal Sonesta in Chicago's River North neighborhood and rebranded it as Hotel 505, signaling the hospitality company's expansion into a new major market. This follows Manga's earlier acquisitions of SoHo 54 and The Chelsean in New York City. The Chicago property sits in a prime downtown location surrounded by dining, entertainment, and cultural attractions.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development. Hotel conversions and acquisitions do not materially affect apartment supply, demand, or construction economics. However, the River North market—a major employment and hospitality corridor—remains competitive for mixed-use development; monitor if hotel capital flight accelerates, which could free up underutilized properties for residential redevelopment.

stories.title: Multifamily, Hospitality CMBS Pose Greatest Refinance Risk in October
stories.excerpt: Refinancing risk for hard maturities in CMBS has shifted from office to multifamily and hospitality this month, Trepp reported. That’s due to a pair of large single-asset single-borrower loans that are severely impaired, carrying a debt yield below 6.0%: a national multifamily portfolio and a Honolulu resort, which together account for 66.79% of the severely impaired balance. In September, retail represented the largest share of severely impaired loans. By share of October hard maturities, office still leads at 27.03%, followed by retail at 22.6% and multifamily at 18.66%. In all, 2026 hard maturities total $76.6 billion, exceeding either of the prior two years, with a back-loaded profile as 39% of the loans are due in the fourth quarter. In total, 19.44% of the cohort balance is in special servicing approaching hard maturity. Unlike September, when office accounted for 74.94% of special-servicing balance, October’s is spread across office (29.71% of all special-servicing balance), retail (29.23%), and multifamily (22.96%), according to Trepp. The post Multifamily, Hospitality CMBS Pose Greatest Refinance Risk in October appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Multifamily & hospitality now largest CMBS refinance risk; 66.79% impairment from two mega-loans.
2026 hard maturities total $76.6B; 39% due Q4; 19.44% of balance in special servicing.
October multifamily in special servicing: 22.96% of total; office down from 74.94% in September.
stories.summary: Refinancing stress has shifted from office to multifamily and hospitality in CMBS, with two severely impaired loans (national multifamily portfolio and Honolulu resort) accounting for two-thirds of the impaired balance. Total 2026 hard maturities reach $76.6 billion, back-loaded toward Q4, with 19.44% of the cohort balance now in special servicing across multiple asset classes. Multifamily accounts for 22.96% of special-servicing balance in October.
stories.impact: Significant refinance wall approaching for multifamily CMBS in 2026—likely forcing distressed sales, yield compression, and cap-rate pressure across the sector. Developers with fixed-rate construction financing and strong balance sheets can acquire stabilized properties and ground-up sites at discounts from stressed sellers. Monitor for price discovery in 4Q 2026; acquisitions ahead of maturity spike will yield highest returns. Refinance failures may also constrain new construction starts if debt markets remain tight.

stories.title: Casa Grande Advances 954-Acre Data Center Campus
stories.excerpt: LKY Development Company was greenlit by a Casa Grande planning agency to develop a 954-acre data center campus at Montgomery Road and Maricopa-Casa Grande Highway. Casa Grande is between Phoenix and Tucson. AZBEX reports LKY is looking for a buyer to purchase the Grande Valley Industrial site and take over development. The project will incorporate low- to zero-ongoing water consumption cooling technologies, sustainable building practices, and low-emission/de minimis on-site electrical generation. As currently designed, the campus is not anticipated to rely on a traditional electric grid connection for primary power service. Bloom Energy will handle the power generation component. The project will feature multiple data center buildings, on-site natural gas power generation and a battery energy storage system. The data centers will incorporate now-standard closed-loop cooling systems to minimize water use and environmental impacts. Development is planned in two phases. The post Casa Grande Advances 954-Acre Data Center Campus appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: LKY Development greenlit to build 954-acre data center campus in Casa Grande, Arizona.
Campus spans Montgomery Road & Maricopa-Casa Grande Highway, between Phoenix and Tucson.
Bloom Energy & battery storage power generation; closed-loop cooling; LKY seeking buyer for development.
stories.summary: LKY Development won approval from Casa Grande planning for a 954-acre data center campus on the Phoenix–Tucson corridor. The project incorporates Bloom Energy on-site generation, battery storage, and closed-loop cooling to minimize water and grid dependence. LKY is actively seeking a buyer to take over development and operations.
stories.impact: Major data center development signal for Arizona Sun Belt corridor. Data centers drive indirect multifamily demand through job creation (construction workers, permanent tech/operations staff, ancillary services) and corporate in-migration. Casa Grande location is strategic for Phoenix metro—monitor for tech talent influx to Phoenix, Tempe, and Scottsdale multifamily markets. If development accelerates, expect renter demand uplift and pricing power in 3–5 mile radius and tech-hub corridors (Phoenix central, Scottsdale North).

stories.title: Waterton Acquires 453-Unit City Walk at Woodbury in MN
stories.excerpt: Waterton has acquired City Walk at Woodbury, a 453-unit rental community in Woodbury, Minnesota. The wrap-style rental community comprises two four-story residential buildings, heated indoor parking garages, a clubhouse and 24,000 square feet of retail space. Waterton will execute a targeted value-add program to enhance the residences, hallways and common areas throughout the community. Built in phases in 2005 and 2011, City Walk at Woodbury features relatively large floor plans across one-, two- and three-bedroom configurations. Waterton plans to execute a tailored approach to residential improvements. Updates will range from refreshed cabinets, hardware, and lighting fixtures to new appliances, countertops, plumbing fixtures, flooring, and paint, as needed. The community is served by the highly-regarded Stillwater Public School District, while proximity to retail, dining and entertainment options offers added convenience. Nearby options for outdoor recreation include Lake Elmo Park Preserve, Powers Lake Park and Lake St. Croix. The post Waterton Acquires 453-Unit City Walk at Woodbury in MN appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Waterton acquires City Walk at Woodbury, 453-unit wrap-style community in Minnesota.
Built 2005–2011; two 4-story buildings, heated parking, 24K SF retail; serves Stillwater school district.
Waterton executes targeted value-add: unit refreshes, appliances, finishes; outdoor recreation proximity near lakes.
stories.summary: Waterton has acquired City Walk at Woodbury, a 453-unit multifamily community in suburban Minneapolis (Woodbury, Minnesota) built in two phases between 2005 and 2011. The property features large floor plans (1-, 2-, 3-bedroom), heated parking, and 24,000 square feet of integrated retail. Waterton plans a targeted value-add renovation of interiors and common areas.
stories.impact: Value-add acquisition in stable Minneapolis suburb signals continued capital deployment into secondary-tier Sun Belt and Midwest markets where cap rates offer modest spread over CMBS refi risk. Woodbury is high-income, school-district-driven suburban market—renovation play likely targets modest rent growth via unit premiumization. No demand or supply shock; typical portfolio management activity.

stories.title: Gantry Secures $16M for Seattle’s Russell Hall Mixed Use in University District
stories.excerpt: Gantry has secured a $16 million permanent loan to refinance maturing debt for Russell Hall, a mixed-use property located at 1414 NE 42nd St, directly adjacent to the University of Washington and “The Ave” retail and hospitality corridor. The 62,400-square-foot, six-story building features 120 subterranean parking stalls, ground floor retail, three floors of office space, and 30 apartment units on the top two floors, including a mix of studio, one-, and two-bedroom floor plans. Ground floor retail includes restaurant options and ready pedestrian access to nearby shopping, dining and academic amenities. Gantry’s Mike Wood, Principal, Mike Taylor, Principal, and Tim Brown, Senior Associate, with the firm’s Seattle production office, represented the borrower, a private real estate investor. The five-year, fixed-rate, non-recourse loan was secured from one of Gantry’s correspondent life companies and offers partial-term interest-only terms. Gantry will service the loan for the lender. The post Gantry Secures $16M for Seattle’s Russell Hall Mixed Use in University District appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Gantry closes $16M permanent loan for Russell Hall, University of Washington adjacent mixed-use.
62.4K SF, 6-story: 120 parking, ground retail, 3 office floors, 30 apartments (top 2 floors).
Five-year fixed, non-recourse, partial I-O from life-insurance correspondent; U-District 'The Ave' retail corridor.
stories.summary: Gantry secured a $16 million permanent refinancing loan for Russell Hall, a mixed-use property at 1414 NE 42nd Street directly adjacent to the University of Washington and The Ave retail corridor. The six-story, 62,400-square-foot building includes 30 apartment units (studios, 1-, 2-bedrooms), ground-floor retail, three office floors, and 120 parking stalls. The five-year, fixed-rate, non-recourse loan was sourced from a life-insurance correspondent.
stories.impact: Limited multifamily relevance; 30 units is incidental to the mixed-use project. However, U-District market remains supply-constrained and high-demand due to UW employment and student population. Successful permanent financing of small-unit mixed-use near campus signals continued lender appetite for university-proximate retail + residential. Developers targeting U-District should note that 'The Ave' retail + residential combinations can attract institutional debt; monitor for larger ground-up opportunities in adjacent parcels.

stories.title: Terra-Led JV Lands $507M Construction Loan for South Beach Condo Before Pre-Sales
stories.excerpt: A Terra-led partnership has scored a $507 million construction loan for a waterfront condo tower in Miami Beach — even before launching sales. The financing from Adi Chugh’s Tyko Capital covers the 28-story, 106-unit development at 1250 West Avenue, along South Beach’s western waterfront facing Biscayne Bay. In an unusual move for a luxury condo development in South Florida, pre-sales will start next year. Typically, lenders require developments to hit a certain sales threshold before they will provide construction financing. “Miami Beach continues to be one of the most supply-constrained luxury markets in the country, and opportunities to build on the bay at this scale are rare,” Chugh said in a statement. Tyko Capital’s debt platform is backed by financial heavyweight Elliott Management. The development will replace a 15-story condo building that was built in 1964. Terra, led by David Martin, bought out the 238-unit building for $120 million last year, The Real Deal reported. (Developer Michael Stern is no longer involved in the project.) To receive approval for the 330-foot-tall tower from Miami Beach officials, the developers also acquired and demolished the Bikini Hostel across the street, with plans to turn it into a public park. The luxury condo development, which does not have a brand attached, will include rooftop pools, an underground parking garage, a padel court, and ground-floor retail space. The development partners include GV Development, the firm of Italian influencer Gianluca Vacchi, LORE Development Group, the Miami-based partnership between Leste Group and Brazilian real estate fund Opportunity Fundo de Investimento Imobiliário, as well as Rafi Gibly’s RG Development Group. The project adds to Terra’s track record in Miami Beach, where it’s building the 800-room hotel next door to the convention center after landing a $392 million loan, also from Tyko Capital. bullets: Terra-led JV secures $507M construction loan for 106-unit luxury condo tower, Miami Beach waterfront.
28-story at 1250 West Avenue, South Beach; pre-sales begin 2025; replaces 1964 15-story building.
Tyko Capital debt platform backed by Elliott Management; rare bay-front development opportunity in supply-constrained market.
stories.summary: A Terra-led partnership closed $507 million in construction financing from Tyko Capital (backed by Elliott Management) for a 28-story, 106-unit luxury condo tower at 1250 West Avenue, Miami Beach, overlooking Biscayne Bay. Unusually, the lender is advancing debt before pre-sales launch (scheduled for 2025), reflecting strong confidence in the South Beach market. The project demolishes a 1964, 15-story, 238-unit building.
stories.impact: Strong signal on Miami Beach luxury-condo financing appetite and capital redeployment. The advance of construction capital absent pre-sales thresholds indicates lender confidence in Bay-front scarcity and South Florida's continued appeal to high-net-worth buyers. However, demolition of a 238-unit 1990s building (implying ~160 units loss if net) for 106 luxury units is net-negative for workforce/middle-income supply. South Beach remains constrained for affordable multifamily; this project reinforces luxury-only development trend and may accelerate pressure on class-B/C stock. Developers should note renewed appetite for waterfront Florida debt; rate/term refinance risk in established communities may offer acquisition opportunities.

stories.title: TJ Maxx Signs 29K-SF Deal to Replace H&M at 150 East 86th Street
stories.excerpt: Discount department store T.J. Maxx is replacing H&M in a busy retail spread on Manhattan’s Upper East Side, Commercial Observer has learned. T.J. Maxx has signed a lease for 28,837 square feet at Extell Development’s retail condominium unit at 150 East 86th Street, according to a source close to the deal and a third-quarter Manhattan retail report from CBRE. The big-box store will replace Sweden-based apparel chain H&M in the space in late 2027, taking over approximately 4,000 square feet on the ground floor and roughly 25,000 square feet on the second floor. Ripco Real Estate’s Richard Skulnik brokered the deal for both T.J. Maxx and Extell. The length of the lease and the asking rent were not disclosed, but CBRE’s report found retail rents on the Upper East Side averaged $259 per square foot during the third quarter of 2026. Extell bought the retail condo unit along East 86th Street from Vornado Realty Trust for $64 million in July 2025. Spokespeople for Extell and T.J. Maxx did not immediately respond to requests for comment. News of T.J. Maxx’s new lease comes about eight months after the retailer signed its first Manhattan lease in nearly a decade at JEMB Realty’s Herald Towers, where it took 40,000 square feet for a term of 10 years. That store at 50 West 34th Street will open by the end of this year. Skulnik also repped T.J. Maxx in that lease. T.J. Maxx will join plenty of nearby retailers on its new Upper East Side block between Lexington and Third avenues, including Target, Old Navy, Foot Locker, Victoria’s Secret and Ulta Beauty. The retailer’s East 86th Street deal was also the largest retail lease signed in Manhattan during the third quarter of this year, followed by Five Iron Golf‘s 28,288-square-foot deal at 32 Old Slip in the Financial District and Crunch Fitness‘ 28,100-square-foot lease at 2192 Broadway on the Upper West Side, according to CBRE. Isabelle Durso can be reached at idurso@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: T.J. Maxx signs 28.8K SF lease, Upper East Side Manhattan retail at 150 East 86th Street.
Replaces H&M in Extell retail condo; 4K SF ground floor, 25K SF second floor; occupancy late 2027.
Market rent ~$259/SF (Q3 2026); Extell purchased unit from Vornado for $64M in July 2025.
stories.summary: T.J. Maxx signed a lease for 28,837 square feet at Extell Development's retail condo at 150 East 86th Street on Manhattan's Upper East Side, replacing H&M. The big-box discount retailer will occupy ~4,000 square feet on the ground floor and ~25,000 square feet on the second floor, with occupancy targeted for late 2027. Upper East Side retail rents averaged $259 per square foot in Q3 2026.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. Retail tenancy churn does not affect apartment supply or demand. However, Upper East Side market dynamics (discount retail replacing apparel flagship) may signal shifting consumer foot traffic and demographic tenant mix—possible headwind for luxury multifamily rents if the area slides downmarket. Also note: Extell's acquisition of retail condo from Vornado for $64M (July 2025) reflects continued capital deployment into trophy Manhattan retail—monitor Extell's real estate portfolio strategy for future mixed-use or residential redevelopment near high-traffic retail nodes.

stories.title: Dwight Capital Refis Pennsylvania Apartments With $34M HUD Loan
stories.excerpt: Vanguard Development has landed $34 million of U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)-backed debt to refinance a multifamily property in south-central Pennsylvania, Commercial Observer has learned. Dwight Capital closed the HUD 223(f) loan backed by the Reserve at Willow Ridge apartment community in Lancaster, Pa., about 65 miles west of Downtown Philadelphia. Brandon Baksh and Noah Greenwald originated the transaction for Dwight. Loan proceeds will be used to fund a replacement reserve account for future capital improvements and return equity to the borrower, built up through the construction, lease-up and stabilization phases, according to Dwight. The 160-unit project debuted in 2023. Located at 110 Summit Drive, the Reserve at Willow Ridge consists of 72 garden-style apartments and 88 townhouse units across 24 buildings. Amenities include a swimming pool, a clubhouse, a fitness center, a picnic pavilion and walking trails. Vanguard Development did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Dwight Capital closes $34M HUD 223(f) refi for Reserve at Willow Ridge, Lancaster, Pennsylvania.
160-unit stabilized project (2023 delivery): 72 garden-style, 88 townhouse units; 24 buildings.
Loan funds replacement reserves & equity return; property 65 miles west of Philadelphia.
stories.summary: Vanguard Development closed a $34 million HUD 223(f) loan through Dwight Capital to refinance the Reserve at Willow Ridge, a 160-unit multifamily community in Lancaster, Pennsylvania (65 miles west of Philadelphia). The property, delivered in 2023, comprises 72 garden-style units and 88 townhouse units across 24 buildings. Loan proceeds fund a replacement-reserve account and return equity accumulated during construction, lease-up, and stabilization.
stories.impact: HUD refinancing availability signals continued lender appetite for stabilized, recently-delivered multifamily outside major metros. Lancaster market (South Central PA) is secondary tier; successful HUD refi suggests moderate fundamentals and operator track record. Developers should note HUD 223(f) as viable refinance/equity-recycle tool for stabilized class-B/C assets in smaller metros—enables return of equity to sponsors for reinvestment in new ground-up deals. No demand/supply implications; routine capital-stack management.

stories.title: Toll Brothers Buys West Chelsea Development Site for $45M
stories.excerpt: It looks like there’s more luxury housing coming to Manhattan’s swanky West Chelsea neighborhood. Homebuilder Toll Brothers, through its Toll Brothers City Living condo development division, has acquired a development site at 126-128 10th Avenue and next-door 456 West 18th Street from longtime owner the Nanis family for a total of $45 million, broker Adirondack Capital Partners announced Thursday. The assembled properties — which cover 8,738 square feet of land — adjoin 118 10th Avenue, a vacant lot which Toll Brothers acquired in February for $53 million with the intention of developing a condo building on the site. Toll Brothers filed plans with the New York City Department of Buildings on Oct. 5 to build a 240,000-square-foot property with 105 units and roughly 20,000 square feet of commercial space at 118 10th Avenue. Amenities designed by CookFox will include a pool, a sauna, a cold plunge and a playroom, according to The Real Deal. The exact plans for the two nearby properties that are part of Toll Brothers’ most recent purchase were unclear. The sites currently hold low-rise buildings, including the now-closed Star on 18 Diner, which is set to be demolished. “This closing builds on our earlier sale of 118 10th Avenue and advances a significant development assemblage in one of Manhattan’s most distinctive residential neighborhoods,” Michael Hunter Coghill, founder and managing partner of Adirondack Capital Partners, said in a statement. “Together, these transactions reflect the value of scarce development opportunities and the persistence required to bring a complex assemblage to closing.” Adirondack Capital Partners’ Coghill, Chad Sinsheimer and Brittany Feinberg brokered the deal. bullets: Toll Brothers City Living buys 8.7K SF West Chelsea development site for $45M.
126–128 10th Ave & 456 West 18th Street; adjoins 118 10th Ave (acquired Feb for $53M).
Plans filed Oct 5: 240K SF, 105 units, 20K SF commercial; designed by CookFox; pool, sauna, plunge.
stories.summary: Toll Brothers City Living acquired two contiguous development parcels at 126–128 10th Avenue and 456 West 18th Street in Manhattan's West Chelsea neighborhood for $45 million, assembling 8,738 square feet of land. The purchase adjoins 118 10th Avenue, which Toll Brothers acquired in February for $53 million. Plans filed in October project a 240,000-square-foot, 105-unit condo development with 20,000 square feet of commercial space and luxury amenities (pool, sauna, cold plunge, playroom).
stories.impact: Major luxury condo land assembly in prime Manhattan micro-market signals continued appetite for high-end residential in West Chelsea despite broader NYC office vacancy. Toll Brothers' sequential acquisitions ($53M + $45M = $98M for ~9K SF) imply ~$10.8K per buildable SF land cost—elevated but justified by waterfront/district adjacency. Land sales indicate landowner willingness to monetize at current pricing; monitor whether additional parcel sales accelerate in West Chelsea. For multifamily developers: luxury Manhattan condo consolidation may limit ground-up multifamily opportunities in high-value neighborhoods; consider value-add repositioning of older rental stock as counter-strategy.

stories.title: AI Platform Synthesia Moves HQ to 50K SF at GFP’s 675 Avenue of the Americas
stories.excerpt: Artificial intelligence companies are continuing to scoop up Midtown’s premiere office space. AI video platform Synthesia, which provides an enterprise-focused communications platform backed by “Shark Tank” entrepreneur Mark Cuban, inked a 50,000-square-foot lease at GFP Real Estate’s 675 Avenue of the Americas for its new U.S. headquarters, according to tenant broker Lee & Associates. The company will relocate to the Flatiron District building between West 21st and West 22nd streets from the Moinian Group’s 245 Fifth Avenue in NoMad, where it signed a lease for 13,600 square feet in August 2025. It is unclear when the move will take place, but the relocation will nearly quadruple Synthesia’s office space in New York City and allow it to expand its headcount, according to Lee & Associates. “Synthesia’s new offices will be designed to enhance both the employee and customer experience, with meeting and collaboration areas, flexible event space, and a studio where customers can create custom avatars, conduct proof-of-concept work and collaborate on video programs,” GFP said in a statement. The length of the lease and the asking rent were not disclosed. The average asking rent for office space in Midtown South was $79.57 per square foot during the third quarter of 2026, according to Colliers research. Dennis Someck and Justin Myers from Lee & Associates represented Synthesia in the deal. Jeffrey Gural and Alphie Toro from GFP, as well as Anthony Sciacca and Scott Gutnick from Newmark, represented the landlord. The brokers did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. 675 Avenue of the Americas is a six-story office building built in 1901 a block west of the landmark Flatiron Building. Other tenants in the building include billing platform Candid Health and commercial real estate data sourcing platform Compstak. bullets: Synthesia, AI video platform, leases 50K SF at 675 Avenue of the Americas for U.S. HQ.
Relocates from Moinian's 245 Fifth Avenue (13.6K SF); quadruples footprint; moves from NoMad to Flatiron.
Backed by Mark Cuban; enables headcount expansion, customer collaboration studio, proof-of-concept space.
stories.summary: Synthesia, an enterprise AI video platform backed by entrepreneur Mark Cuban, signed a 50,000-square-foot lease at GFP Real Estate's 675 Avenue of the Americas (Flatiron District, between 21st–22nd Streets) for its new U.S. headquarters. The company is relocating from 13,600 square feet at Moinian Group's 245 Fifth Avenue in NoMad, nearly quadrupling its footprint to accommodate headcount expansion and new customer collaboration and studio spaces.
stories.impact: Meaningful employment growth signal for Flatiron/Midtown South Manhattan. AI company headcount expansion (implied by 3.7x footprint increase) drives ancillary services demand and worker migration into nearby neighborhoods. Monitor for downstream multifamily demand in Flatiron, NoMad, and East Village as Synthesia and peer AI/tech firms expand payrolls. Company relocations from NoMad to Flatiron suggest gradual tech-hub migration eastward and southward—multifamily developers should track Flatiron/Gramercy rents and occupancy; may signal premium rents and pricing power in submarkets near major tech-employer concentration.
